title: From finite feasibility to a uniform row point
statement: Let $X, Y \subseteq \bbr$ together with a payoff function $f : \bbr \to \bbr \to \bbr$ satisfy the convex-compact minimax hypotheses, and let $c \in \bbr$. Suppose that for every finite subset $u \subseteq Y$ the set $X \cap \bigcap_{y \in u} \mathrm{sublevel}(X,f,y,c)$ is nonempty, where $\mathrm{sublevel}(X,f,y,c) = X \cap \{x \in \bbr : f(x,y) \le c\}$; that is, there is a common row point $x \in X$ with $f(x,y) \le c$ for all $y$ in that finite set. Then there exists a single $x \in X$ with $f(x,y) \le c$ for every $y \in Y$.
hypotheses_covered: X, Y and f satisfy the convex-compact minimax hypotheses
for every finite subset u ⊆ Y, the intersection of X with the minimax sublevel sets over u is nonempty
replaced:
Under \texttt{OnlineLearning.ConvexCompactMinimaxHypotheses}, let $c \in \bbr$.
If for every finite subset $u \subseteq Y$ there exists $x \in X$ with
$f(x,y) \leq c$ for all $y \in u$, then there exists $x \in X$ with
$f(x,y) \leq c$ for \emph{all} $y \in Y$.
